_about: Criterion dictionary for tools/wem_lint.py — the controlled vocabulary of CODE
IDENTIFIERS the NFR lint measures src/wattleflow against, for the
translating tools/naming_registry.yaml — which the tool stopped reading in
v1.4.0/1.5.0 when the criterion moved to JSON, leaving this distribution with
no machine-readable criterion of its own. The YAML file stays on disk until
DR-PRC-001 retires it, but it is NO LONGER the source of truth. It replaces a
verbatim copy of the workflow criterion, which declared another distribution's
domains and tier and could only have measured this tree by accident.
JSON, not YAML: the lint is stdlib-only by design, and json is the only
structured format the standard library parses. Keys starting with an
underscore are prose and are dropped by the loader.
Presentation (report strings, finding catalogue) is NOT here: it lives in the
instrument's own tools/messages.json, shared by every distribution, versioned
apart from this criterion and outside the D-10 triple.
The registry describes the TARGET state, not the state of the tree: the tool
measures how far the source deviates from it. Every extension — a new domain,
subject, operation, acronym or TypeVar role — requires a DR record.

and `subjects` the same three; `identifier_acronyms` gains `RSS`. Before

non-grouping package), so the first RSS pipeline would have gone unmeasured.

0.8.0 (2026-09-03) — `audit.info_exempt` gains `DriverLocalStorage`.
The rule reads a driver as a step inside somebody else's unit of work and
bars `self.info()` outright; it cannot tell a record that scales with the
INPUT (one per write) from one that scales with the RUN (one at load, one
tally at close). The driver now emits the second kind only: where it writes
and under what policy when it loads, and read/written/copied/bytes when the
workflow asks it to report. Per-operation records stay at DEBUG.
Cost: the exemption is by CLASS, so nothing stops a later `self.info()` in
a loop of this same class from passing unmeasured. Refining the rule to see
call context instead of class membership is the alternative, and it is the
question the DR has to settle.
Measured, not predicted: OBS-03 goes 3 -> 1 with this entry (the two new
driver records), and the remaining finding is the pre-existing one in
`WriteEmailCopyOLD`. No other rule moves, so vectors stay comparable with
0.7.0 for every rule except OBS-03.

_python_reference: Defines the 'stdlib' set for ORG-01; must track requires-python in pyproject.toml.
_acronym_identifier_casing: Enforcement level of the acronym-casing criterion — a registry fact under DR
governance rather than a constant in the tool: `adopted` makes the check an
ERROR, any other status falls back to the severity declared for the
`acronym_case` rule below. DR-WFL-004 (PDF vs Pdf) is open, so it warns.

acronym_identifier_casing.note: the lint warns (WARNING, waiver declared) instead of failing the build until the decision is taken

_blind_spots: Declared unmeasured territory. Reported as INFO on every run so the vector can
blind_spots: imports inside the shared namespace are not modelled as edges, so cycles and layering within helpers/ are unmeasured (helpers->domain acyclicity and helper fan-in ARE measured)

the helpers/ tree of this distribution merges with the workflow one at runtime (PEP 420); the lint sees only the modules under this --src, so a fan-in count here is a lower bound over the merged namespace

ORG-01 criterion 1 counts consumer domains, which is not evidence of where a module belongs: a cross-cutting CAPABILITY (NFRQ-ORG-04, CLAUDE.md 2.6) and a module implementing a core contract keep their home in helpers/ whatever the current fan-in says. Serialisation is the standing example — a Formatter is an IFormatter specialisation (core) callable from a pipeline transformation just as much as from a write strategy, so `helpers.formatters` reading as single-consumer is a snapshot of today's callers, not a misplacement. A K4 finding is a question about the module, never an instruction to relocate it.
ORG-01 measures the import graph, never the runtime one: dynamic edges (WorkflowFactory registry, YAML-declared types) are invisible to the AST
the pipelines/nlp package is exempt from the name grammar (the 44% named-entity cluster, NFRQ-ORG-02 Appendix A §1) — its names are unmeasured by construction
third-party dependencies are declared here as a tier, but this distribution ships no SBOM or hash-pinned lock yet (NFRQ-SEC-03 criterion 4), so tier membership is a claim, not an attestation
a strategic adversary is beyond the reach of the lint
NFRQ-OBS-01 criteria 4 and 5 (WARNING is never a failure; CRITICAL means the component cannot continue) need the semantics of the branch and are not machine-decidable — reviewed, not measured
NFRQ-OBS-02 criterion 2 (entry and exit of one operation share `msg` and differ only in `step`) is reviewed: pairing two calls as one operation is not decidable from the AST alone
NFRQ-OBS-03 criterion 2 measures records per unit of work at RUNTIME; the static lint cannot see it, so the [M] value is absent from this vector, not zero
_rules: The rule table as the NFR registry declares it: id, requirement, check,
severity and waiver policy. The tool resolves severity from here (POLICY §9).
`clean_core_imports` is WARNING in this distribution, not ERROR:
wattleflow-processors is the NON-core tier — third-party is legitimate here,
so the check measures departure from the DECLARED tier and feeds a migration
worklist (the ORG-01 tolerance policy) rather than blocking a build.
_domains: NFRQ-ORG-01 — top-level functional packages under src/wattleflow owned by this
distribution. `helpers` is the shared namespace, NOT a domain: it must not
appear here, or intra-helper imports get misreported as acyclicity breaks.
`enums` is likewise absent (2026-08-22, DR-WFL-016): like `constants` in the
clean core it imports nothing intra-project, so it is foundation material every
layer — helpers included — may depend on. Declaring it a domain turned three
helper->enums imports into ORG-01 leaf errors.
_report_language: Default report language; --lang overrides it per run. Presentation, not criterion (D-13).
_scope: Distribution tier. wattleflow-processors is the NON-core distribution: it is
the home of third-party-bound modules (NFRQ-SEC-03) — but 'non-core' is not
'anything goes'. `core_libraries` declares the tier this distribution INTENDS
to carry; a module importing outside it is reported (K9) and skipped by the
The LLM/NLP backends (anthropic, huggingface_hub, tqdm, transformers, spacy,
stanza, flair, gliner, torch) ARE in the tier: DR-PRC-001 placed the model
access path in this distribution and carries the masking test as its witness
(huggingface_hub, transformers, tqdm masked -> the modules still import).
The tier is what this distribution imports, so declaring them is describing
it; leaving them out ALSO cost coverage, because the ORG rules skip every
module reported as foreign — seven modules read as clean while unmeasured.
Membership stays a claim, not an attestation, until the distribution ships
an SBOM and a hash-pinned lock (NFRQ-SEC-03 criterion 4) — a declared blind
spot, not a gap this list closes.
`guarded_optional` is the only waiver, and the test is masking (mask the
package — the module must still import and work), never code review.
_distribution_manifest: NFRQ-SEC-03 criteria 2/3 — the packaging manifest of this distribution, read by
the `distribution_manifest` check (stdlib tomllib). `pyproject` is relative to
the repository root (the parent of tools/).
_bases: NFRQ-ORG-02 — inheritance roots. A class belongs to a family if it inherits one
of that family's bases; pipeline detection reads `bases.pipeline`.
_capabilities: NFRQ-ORG-04 — recognised cross-cutting capabilities: callable helpers named by
capability, never specialisations of a domain primitive. First holders:
_pipeline_grammar: package_subject binds the leading facet to the owning package (criterion 5);
grouping_packages relax criterion 5 where one package holds several
subjects; exempt_packages are deferred by DR and skipped entirely.
_synonyms: Operation synonyms collapsed to the canonical verb (NFRQ-ORG-02, DRY).
_identifier_acronyms: Acronym TOKENS as they appear in code identifiers — distinct from the discourse `acronyms` table of documentation/dictionary.yaml.
_prohibited_standalone: Bare generic role nouns prohibited as STANDALONE class names (NFRQ-ORG-02
criterion 6; NFRQ-ORG-04 criterion 3 delegates its capability role-nouns here).
The same noun is legal as a qualified facet — `DriverS3UriParser`, not `Parser`.
_type_vars: NFRQ-ORG-03 — a TypeVar names the SEMANTIC ROLE the type plays in the generic
contract, not the mechanism. Acronym casing is checked against
`identifier_acronyms`. `tolerated` holds branded names awaiting a DR decision
(WARNING, not ERROR, until decided — the ORG-01 tolerance policy); it is
empty, so no branded name is currently carried.
_preset_allowed: NFRQ-ORG-07 — Preset Whitelist Declaration. A class whose optional runtime
configuration is carried by PresetDecorator declares the permitted keys in a
Why a rule and not a preference: PresetDecorator resolves the whitelist from
the CLASS (`type(parent).ALLOWED`). A declaration under any other name, or at
module scope, is invisible to that resolution — the whitelist reads as empty
and every configuration key the caller passes is dropped WITHOUT ERROR. The
failure is silent by construction, which is why the severity is `error`.
This distribution held 26 of the 27 non-conforming declarations found on
2026-08-01 (4 spellings); they were consolidated in the same change.
_audit: NFRQ-OBS-01/02/03 criterion data: which call is an audit call, which levels escalate, which Event members are phases, and which classes are steps inside a unit of work (and therefore emit no INFO). Editing this block edits the criterion -> DR (D-03).

fields.step: phase of that operation within time
fields.scope: which part of the same operation
fields.component: subsystem or external participant the operation uses
fields.target: the kind of object the operation acts on
fields.reason: why the outcome is what it is — a human sentence

_qualifiers: Qualifier facet of NFRQ-ORG-02, matched one CamelCase segment at a time — a
multi-word entry is unreachable by construction.
Backend/tool names: Spacy, Stanza, Flair, Deberta, Gliner, Tika.
What the operation acts on or produces: Attachment, Spans, Text, Dictionary,
Macro, Sticky, Words, Digest. Container format read: EML, MSG.
`Text` is also a Subject; position decides the facet, so the token is
NOT registered on purpose: `Entity` — the 0.1.0 note keeps it an open
question (whether Entity joins the SUBJECT vocabulary and whether
Entities/EntityRecognition collapse into it), and registering it here as a
qualifier would close that question sideways.
_exempt_packages: Packages the pipeline grammar skips entirely (NFRQ-ORG-02 Appendix A). An
exemption is a debt: it must protect something, and it must be visible (K17,
D-11). Measured 2026-08-24 by lifting each one in turn — only `nlp` is
load-bearing (13 names become ERROR without it, the named-entity cluster).
`rss` and `xml` hold no module but __init__.py, and `quality` holds no
Pipeline class at all, so their exemptions protected nothing and merely made
the list disagree with the blind spot, which names `nlp` alone.
Do not pre-emptively exempt a package: declare the exemption when a name
actually needs it, through a DR.
